subject: Competitive packaging alignment — Bridgerow / ApexCloud comparison
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@bridgerow.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive offer — need alignment and packaging clarifications

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. We received a commercial offer from ApexCloud that materially undercuts list on the first-year term and includes a 6-week pilot credit, plus a small implementation stipend. Before we take this to procurement for final review, can Redwood provide:

- A short comparison / gap list vs. the ApexCloud proposal (pricing and key commercial levers).
- Whether you can match the headline unit price for the pilot window or instead provide an equivalent credit.
- Clarification on Private deployment options (we require VPC with customer-managed networking), SSO via Okta, and data residency in the US.
- Any standard PS/implementation estimate for a 10-engineer integration (we are targeting GA in Q3).

I attached Apex_Offer_Summary.pdf from their email so you have the exact numbers. Procurement is the final decision-maker; if we can get a clean commercial and MAP (mutual action plan) this week, it helps us move faster.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Lee
Head of Cloud Integrations
Bridgerow Inc.

Attachments: Apex_Offer_Summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@bridgerow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive offer — need alignment and packaging clarifications

Hannah — thanks for sending this and for the detail. We reviewed the Apex summary and sketched three defensible concession scenarios depending on how Bridgerow wants to balance cash vs. time-to-value:

1) Pilot-credit parity (lowest friction): match Apex pilot economics for first 6 weeks with a consumption credit, no long-term list price change. Requires a signed MAP and PS statement of work.

2) Term discount (commit): 8% off list on a 12-month committed consumption band + 4 weeks pilot credit. Requires 12-month minimum commit and standard SLA addendum.

3) Hybrid (preferred for larger adoption): One-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 6 weeks) + 4% list discount + 30% reduced PS rate for first engagement.

A few clarifying asks so we model the numbers precisely:
- Can you confirm expected average sequence length & peak QPS for the pilot?
- Confirm that production must be Private (VPC) for the term or if Hosted w/ VPC peering is acceptable for pilot.
- Any internal billing constraints (PO timing or merchant vs. invoice)?

I attached an initial_concession_matrix.xlsx with ballpark $ impacts for each option and the PS day estimates. Connor — can you confirm the PS day assumptions and whether the VPC deployment timeline matches their 6–8 week window?

If we get those details by EOD tomorrow, we can push a draft commercial term sheet and MAP back to procurement for signature.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial_concession_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@bridgerow.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Bridgerow Procurement <procurement@bridgerow.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive offer — need alignment and packaging clarifications

Dylan — thanks, that framing is helpful. Quick answers:
- Pilot target: ~25k tokens/day average, expected burst to 200k tokens/day during load tests; steady-state GA estimate is ~1.2M tokens/day.
- Production requirement: must be Private (managed VPC or on-prem bundle) due to data residency and compliance. Hosted with peering is not acceptable for production, but acceptable for a short pilot if we can guarantee the region and ID controls.
- Billing: Procurement prefers invoice-based billing with a standard 60-day payment term and an initial PO.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required, plus standard breach notification timelines.

Procurement has asked for a MAP with milestones (pilot start, pilot completion, production cutover) and a draft commercial term sheet including the pilot credit phrasing and PS estimate. Also, they asked whether Redwood can commit to a 30-day rollback window and an outage credit cap tied to SLA.

Assuming we get the MAP and a matching financial construct by next Wednesday, we will route this through procurement and legal. Can you include a short PS scope (SOW) and high-level timeline in the MAP?

Thanks,
Hannah

On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@bridgerow.com> wrote:
> [see Apex_Offer_Summary.pdf attached]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@bridgerow.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive offer — need alignment and packaging clarifications

Hannah / Dylan — copying in the technical handshake details per Hannah's asks.

Technical/ops commitments we can make (high level):
- Private deployment: VPC-based private control plane deployed into Bridgerow's AWS accounts (us-east-1). Estimated provisioning time: 10 business days after network prep and infra approvals.
- SSO: Okta integration supported; we will deliver SAML metadata and a test connector within 3 business days of access.
- Data residency & retention: Customer data will remain in-account; retention configurable. We can commit to a 90-day default retention and offer enterprise retention add-on proposals if you need longer.
- PS estimate: 12 PS days for pilot onboarding (networking, SSO, test datasets), 20 PS days for production cutover (runbooks, run-of-service tests). We included a 30% reduced PS rate in the Hybrid option Dylan shared.
- Rollback & SLA: We can support a 30-day rollback plan from cutover with a documented rollback playbook. For SLA credits: standard model is credits based on monthly uptime percentage with a capped credit equal to 25% of monthly fees for major incidents.

Next steps (commercially actionable):
1) Dylan to circulate the MAP + commercial term sheet reflecting one of the concession scenarios.
2) On acceptance of MAP, schedule a 60–90 minute technical kickoff; we will book PS resources.
3) Provide network details (VPC CIDRs, peering/Transit Gateway info) and Okta test account.

If procurement prefers the pilot parity route, the only engineering gating items are the network allowlists and a short VPN/peering config window — we can meet a 6-week pilot start target if approvals are timely.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
